items.claim: The excerpted Holy-One-of-Israel construct fragment is labeled byte tier but its combining-mark order does not reproduce the source bytes.
items.evidence: The row's full-verse citation of the verse is a true byte match, but the separately excerpted construct phrase קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (cited as tier: byte) reorders the sin-dot and sheva combining characters on its second word relative to the source; the fragment matches only at the canonically-normalized level, not the raw byte sequence the tier label claims. This is confined to the one hand-excerpted fragment and does not affect the verse's other correctly-disclosed title object (the separate suffixed epithet earlier in the verse) or the seam claim itself.

items.claim: The rejected-alternative field grounds this verse's isolability in an appeal to the review process's own prior determinations rather than in an argued textual parallel, and the real byte warrant for a doxology-closure pattern goes uncited.
items.evidence: The clause crediting a doxology-closure pattern this campaign has recognized elsewhere in the book names no verse and argues from the reviewing project's own history rather than from bytes. Isaiah's own text does carry the pattern the row is reaching for: the four-word clause כִּֽי נִחַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ עַמּ֔וֹ in this verse is byte-identical to a clause in the doxological call at web:Isa.52.9, and web:Isa.44.23 opens with the same sing-heavens / break-out-mountains verb pair used here, each closing a preceding salvation announcement the way this row treats web:Isa.49.13 as closing the preceding ingathering promise. The row's isolability conclusion is plausible on the bytes, but as written it cites process precedent instead of the parallel that would actually support it.
tier_citations: same verb-pair vocabulary (not claimed byte-identical): oshb:Isa.44.23 vs oshb:Isa.49.13
